# How to get an apostille in Michigan
Short answer: Michigan apostilles come from the Office of the Great Seal, part of the Michigan Department of State. The fee is $1 per document, paid by check or money order to “State of Michigan.” You can mail the request to Lansing or book an office visit. There is no online filing and no expedited service. [source](https://www.michigan.gov/sos/all-services/document-authentication-and-apostille) [source](https://www.michigan.gov/sos/faqs/office-of-the-great-seal/document-authentication)

Michigan issues an apostille for countries in the Hague Apostille Convention and a Certificate of Authority for every other country. Both have the same requirements, fee, and instructions. Michigan won’t issue either one for a document that will be used in the United States. [source](https://www.michigan.gov/sos/all-services/document-authentication-and-apostille)

## Fee, speed, and how to submit

| Item | Michigan rule |
| State fee | $1 per document (the request form says per authentication, not per page). Check or money order payable to the State of Michigan; don’t send cash. [source](https://www.michigan.gov/sos/all-services/document-authentication-and-apostille) [source](https://www.michigan.gov/sos/-/media/Project/Websites/sos/Notary/OGS_AUTHENTICATION_REQUEST_FORM.pdf?rev=ca5c4ec5c20a4ec0a31da36855d6e5c6&hash=BEE3D98ED703927F62A9E6A6C9D18723) |
| Online | Not available. Documents can’t be authenticated or apostilled online or at a self-service station. [source](https://www.michigan.gov/sos/all-services/document-authentication-and-apostille) |
| By mail | Michigan Department of State, Office of the Great Seal, 7064 Crowner Drive, Lansing, MI 48918. [source](https://www.michigan.gov/sos/all-services/document-authentication-and-apostille) |
| In person | By appointment only, through the online appointment system or by calling (888) 767-6424. At the Bureau of Elections, visits are Mondays and Wednesdays, 8:30 a.m. to 4 p.m. [source](https://www.michigan.gov/sos/all-services/document-authentication-and-apostille) |
| Processing time | The FAQ says turnaround is 1 to 2 weeks. [source](https://www.michigan.gov/sos/all-services/document-authentication-and-apostille) The current request form (Rev. 8/23) says to allow 4 to 6 weeks after the office receives it, plus mail time. [source](https://www.michigan.gov/sos/-/media/Project/Websites/sos/Notary/OGS_AUTHENTICATION_REQUEST_FORM.pdf?rev=ca5c4ec5c20a4ec0a31da36855d6e5c6&hash=BEE3D98ED703927F62A9E6A6C9D18723) Plan for the longer figure if you have a deadline. |
| Expedited | Not available. Requests are handled in the order received, and courier, Express, or Priority Mail envelopes are not processed any faster than regular mail. [source](https://www.michigan.gov/sos/faqs/office-of-the-great-seal/document-authentication) [source](https://www.michigan.gov/sos/-/media/Project/Websites/sos/Notary/OGS_AUTHENTICATION_REQUEST_FORM.pdf?rev=ca5c4ec5c20a4ec0a31da36855d6e5c6&hash=BEE3D98ED703927F62A9E6A6C9D18723) |
| Questions | MDOS-Notary@Michigan.gov [source](https://www.michigan.gov/sos/-/media/Project/Websites/sos/Notary/OGS_AUTHENTICATION_REQUEST_FORM.pdf?rev=ca5c4ec5c20a4ec0a31da36855d6e5c6&hash=BEE3D98ED703927F62A9E6A6C9D18723) |

## Which offices can do it in person?
Document authentication is available, by appointment, at the Office of the Great Seal (Richard H. Austin Building, 1st Floor, 430 W. Allegan Street, Lansing) and at eight Secretary of State offices: Clinton Township, Detroit (West Grand Boulevard), Flint (Fenton Road), Grand Rapids (28th Street), Lansing (East Michigan Avenue), Livonia, Marquette, and Pontiac. [source](https://www.michigan.gov/sos/all-services/document-authentication-and-apostille) [source](https://www.michigan.gov/sos/faqs/office-of-the-great-seal/document-authentication) Book through the Secretary of State appointment system. Bring the signed request form, the $1 per document fee, and the documents. [source](https://www.michigan.gov/sos/all-services/document-authentication-and-apostille)

## Step by step by mail

- Get the right version of the document. Use the table below. Vital records must be certified copies, and anything in a foreign language needs a written English translation. [source](https://www.michigan.gov/sos/all-services/document-authentication-and-apostille)
- Fill out and sign the Authentication Request Form. It asks for your name, phone and email, the return address, the number of documents, and the destination country. For China it also asks whether the document is going to Mainland China, Hong Kong, or Macao. [source](https://www.michigan.gov/sos/-/media/Project/Websites/sos/Notary/OGS_AUTHENTICATION_REQUEST_FORM.pdf?rev=ca5c4ec5c20a4ec0a31da36855d6e5c6&hash=BEE3D98ED703927F62A9E6A6C9D18723)
- Add the fee: a check or money order for $1 per document to the State of Michigan. [source](https://www.michigan.gov/sos/-/media/Project/Websites/sos/Notary/OGS_AUTHENTICATION_REQUEST_FORM.pdf?rev=ca5c4ec5c20a4ec0a31da36855d6e5c6&hash=BEE3D98ED703927F62A9E6A6C9D18723)
- Add a return envelope: a self-addressed, stamped envelope or a prepaid air bill (FedEx, UPS, USPS). On a courier air bill, list yourself as both sender and receiver. [source](https://www.michigan.gov/sos/-/media/Project/Websites/sos/Notary/OGS_AUTHENTICATION_REQUEST_FORM.pdf?rev=ca5c4ec5c20a4ec0a31da36855d6e5c6&hash=BEE3D98ED703927F62A9E6A6C9D18723) The office won’t pay return postage. [source](https://www.michigan.gov/sos/faqs/office-of-the-great-seal/document-authentication)
- Mail everything to 7064 Crowner Drive, Lansing, MI 48918. [source](https://www.michigan.gov/sos/all-services/document-authentication-and-apostille)

## Document rules

| Document | Michigan rule |
| Birth, death, marriage, divorce records | Only certified copies from the county clerk, the State Registrar, or (for Wayne, Oakland, and Macomb counties only) the city clerk. Not copies from court or probate clerks, not notarized vital records, not photocopies, and not records from other states. Don’t notarize the certificate or attach anything to it. [source](https://www.michigan.gov/sos/-/media/Project/Websites/sos/Notary/Birth-Certificate.pdf?rev=8ed74e66574a46c09d978cd70ad817bb&hash=C06DC53466B430B9EEBD31BE7CD60DDD) [source](https://www.michigan.gov/sos/-/media/Project/Websites/sos/Notary/Marriage-License.pdf?rev=25be22542f8141439a425462fb292f2a&hash=796E2A6575DA414956E46AAACDD5EA58) The Great Seal’s instruction sheet also says the record must have been produced within 15 years. [source](https://www.michigan.gov/sos/-/media/Project/Websites/sos/Notary/Birth-Certificate.pdf?rev=8ed74e66574a46c09d978cd70ad817bb&hash=C06DC53466B430B9EEBD31BE7CD60DDD) You can ask the State Registrar (517-335-8666) for a certified copy for use abroad and arrange for it to be mailed straight to the Office of the Great Seal. [source](https://www.michigan.gov/sos/-/media/Project/Websites/sos/Notary/Birth-Certificate.pdf?rev=8ed74e66574a46c09d978cd70ad817bb&hash=C06DC53466B430B9EEBD31BE7CD60DDD) Certified copies are ordered through MDHHS Vital Records. [source](https://www.michigan.gov/sos/faqs/office-of-the-great-seal/document-authentication) |
| Michigan court documents | Must be a Michigan court document. If the copy is certified by the court and a court official, the person named in it adds a signed “true copy” statement in front of a Michigan notary. [source](https://www.michigan.gov/sos/-/media/Project/Websites/sos/Notary/Court-Document.pdf?rev=eb3245895f97456badb4a19e3cea0ccb&hash=580C610BA37047052B7CD08BA6F262D6) |
| Diplomas and transcripts | On your original, write or type “this is my original (name of record)” and sign it in front of a Michigan notary. On a copy, write “this is a true copy of my (name of record)” and sign it the same way. A school official can instead state “this is a true copy,” add their title, and sign in front of a Michigan notary (no signature stamps). The authentication is permanently attached, so you may prefer to use a copy. [source](https://www.michigan.gov/sos/-/media/Project/Websites/sos/Notary/School-Records.pdf?rev=7c7d70fe5dd74fc0a56218a7612f44c6&hash=3AE8327DB756BA4154D794614C19B87C) |
| Criminal background checks | Michigan checks come from the Michigan State Police (including the I-CHAT online tool). If the agency didn’t notarize the record, put a true copy statement on it and sign it before a Michigan notary. [source](https://www.michigan.gov/sos/-/media/Project/Websites/sos/Notary/Criminal-Background-Checks.pdf?rev=d5844264215b405483037ff09158d0d2&hash=7D926F2120A1DFE8D1D1AC5E65AB9E8E) |
| Power of attorney and other signed papers | Signed in front of a Michigan notary, with original signatures. The notary must not be named at the beginning of the document as if attesting to the whole thing, and the notarial block can’t include details about the signer such as address or date of birth. Foreign-language documents need a notarized English translation. [source](https://www.michigan.gov/sos/-/media/Project/Websites/sos/Notary/Power-of-Attorney.pdf?rev=59de6d5ca9de45218d99199f3d1d344f&hash=C5B1F29A72ACE8497074EAC94214B3D3) |
| Articles of incorporation | Certified copies issued by the Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs (LARA). [source](https://www.michigan.gov/sos/all-services/document-authentication-and-apostille) |

## Why a Michigan notary, and what is a “true copy” statement?
Michigan notaries can’t certify that a copy is a true copy. Only the person named on the document (or the person or institution that produced it) can make that statement. The notary then notarizes that person’s signature. [source](https://www.michigan.gov/sos/faqs/office-of-the-great-seal/document-authentication) A parent can sign for someone under 18. [source](https://www.michigan.gov/sos/-/media/Project/Websites/sos/Notary/School-Records.pdf?rev=7c7d70fe5dd74fc0a56218a7612f44c6&hash=3AE8327DB756BA4154D794614C19B87C)
The Office of the Great Seal checks the notarization closely. It must show the notary’s printed name, signature, date, commission expiration date, county of commission, and the county of the act if different. An embosser alone isn’t enough, the whole notarial block must be on one page, and stamped or photocopied notary signatures are rejected. [source](https://www.michigan.gov/sos/all-services/document-authentication-and-apostille) [source](https://www.michigan.gov/sos/-/media/Project/Websites/sos/Notary/Court-Document.pdf?rev=eb3245895f97456badb4a19e3cea0ccb&hash=580C610BA37047052B7CD08BA6F262D6) [source](https://www.michigan.gov/sos/faqs/office-of-the-great-seal/document-authentication)
Documents notarized by an out-of-state notary can’t be authenticated in Michigan. [source](https://www.michigan.gov/sos/-/media/Project/Websites/sos/Notary/Prohibited-Documents.pdf?rev=88ec2c61cdd844a28645943f3fb45789&hash=F88371F110B1599DE13B6D70B0D0267C) If you plan to notarize online, the notary still has to be a Michigan notary for Michigan to apostille it.

## What Michigan won’t authenticate

- Documents notarized by an out-of-state notary, and out-of-country or out-of-state records and vital records. [source](https://www.michigan.gov/sos/-/media/Project/Websites/sos/Notary/Prohibited-Documents.pdf?rev=88ec2c61cdd844a28645943f3fb45789&hash=F88371F110B1599DE13B6D70B0D0267C)
- Business and non-business documents with no tie to Michigan. [source](https://www.michigan.gov/sos/-/media/Project/Websites/sos/Notary/Prohibited-Documents.pdf?rev=88ec2c61cdd844a28645943f3fb45789&hash=F88371F110B1599DE13B6D70B0D0267C)
- U.S. immigration and naturalization paperwork. [source](https://www.michigan.gov/sos/-/media/Project/Websites/sos/Notary/Prohibited-Documents.pdf?rev=88ec2c61cdd844a28645943f3fb45789&hash=F88371F110B1599DE13B6D70B0D0267C)
- Documents to be used in the United States. [source](https://www.michigan.gov/sos/-/media/Project/Websites/sos/Notary/Prohibited-Documents.pdf?rev=88ec2c61cdd844a28645943f3fb45789&hash=F88371F110B1599DE13B6D70B0D0267C)
- Documents that make claims about citizenship, immunity, allegiance, or sovereignty, or that use “Notario Publico” or “Notaria Publica.” [source](https://www.michigan.gov/sos/-/media/Project/Websites/sos/Notary/Prohibited-Documents.pdf?rev=88ec2c61cdd844a28645943f3fb45789&hash=F88371F110B1599DE13B6D70B0D0267C)

## Non-Hague countries
For a country outside the Hague Convention, Michigan issues a Certificate of Authority. The Great Seal notes that many of these countries only accept documents certified at both the state and federal levels, so expect a further step at the U.S. Department of State and possibly the embassy. [source](https://www.michigan.gov/sos/all-services/document-authentication-and-apostille) See apostille versus authentication and apostille by country.
Rather not do this yourself?
Tell us the document, that it was issued in Michigan, and where it's going. We'll pass your request to an independent apostille service that can handle the whole thing, and they'll reply with a quote. It's free to ask and you're under no obligation.
Get it done for me
You can also start a request with Apostille-USA. Use the link that matches your document:

- Apostille-USA, original document
- Apostille-USA, true (certified) copy
See the affiliate disclosure for how those links work.

# How to get an apostille in Missouri
Short answer: The Missouri Secretary of State charges $10 per apostille, authentication, or certification, counted per notary or official on the document. Walk-in customers in Jefferson City can get same-day processing, and the St. Louis, Kansas City, and Springfield branch offices provide the service too. Mailed documents are given same-day or next-day service, according to the state’s Notary Handbook. [source](https://www.sos.mo.gov/Business/Notary/notary/certify) [source](https://www.sos.mo.gov/CMSImages/Business/Notary/NotaryHandbook.pdf)

The Secretary of State’s Notaries & Commissions Unit confirms that a Missouri official, such as a notary public, recorder of deeds, circuit clerk, judge, county clerk, or the State Registrar, had the authority to sign your document. The country where the document will be used decides which certificate is attached. [source](https://www.sos.mo.gov/Business/Notary/notary/certify)

## At a glance

| Item | What the official page says |
| Fee | $10 per certification or authentication (including an apostille). [source](https://www.sos.mo.gov/Business/Notary/notary/certify) [source](https://www.sos.mo.gov/CMSImages/Business/Notary/CoverLetterComplete.pdf) |
| Adoptions | State law caps the fee for certain adoption documents at $100 per child per adoption, or per group of children adopted at the same time. [source](https://www.sos.mo.gov/Business/Notary/notary/certify) |
| Payment | Check or money order payable to the Secretary of State’s Office, or MasterCard, Visa, American Express, or Discover using the credit card payment sheet. Card payments carry a small convenience fee. [source](https://www.sos.mo.gov/Business/Notary/notary/certify) [source](https://www.sos.mo.gov/CMSImages/Business/Notary/CreditCardPaymentSheet.pdf) |
| Where to send it | Commissions, Secretary of State’s Office, 600 West Main, Room 322, Jefferson City, MO 65101 [source](https://www.sos.mo.gov/Business/Notary/notary/certify) [source](https://www.sos.mo.gov/CMSImages/Business/Notary/CoverLetterComplete.pdf) |
| Walk-in | Same-day processing for walk-in customers, 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., at 600 W. Main St., Room 322, Jefferson City [source](https://www.sos.mo.gov/CMSImages/Business/Notary/NotaryHandbook.pdf) |
| Branch offices | St. Louis: 815 Olive St., Ste. 150 (314-340-7490). Kansas City: 615 E. 13th St., Ste. 513 (816-889-2925). Springfield: 149 Park Central Sq., Ste. 624 (417-895-6330). [source](https://www.sos.mo.gov/CMSImages/Business/Notary/NotaryHandbook.pdf) |
| Mail processing | Documents received in the mail are given same-day or next-day service. [source](https://www.sos.mo.gov/CMSImages/Business/Notary/NotaryHandbook.pdf) |
| Phone | (573) 751-2783, or toll-free (866) 223-6535 [source](https://www.sos.mo.gov/CMSImages/Business/Notary/CoverLetterComplete.pdf) |

## How the $10 fee is counted
Missouri charges by the official being verified, document by document. The Secretary of State gives these examples: [source](https://www.sos.mo.gov/Business/Notary/notary/certify)

- One document with several notarizations, all by the same notary: $10.
- Several documents, all notarized by the same notary: $10 per document.
- One document notarized by several different notaries: $10 per notary.

## Apostille, authentication, or certification?

| Certificate | What it verifies |
| Certification | A Missouri notary public. |
| Authentication | A recorder of deeds, circuit clerk, judge, county clerk, or the State Registrar (for example on a birth certificate, marriage statement, or divorce statement). |
| Apostille | The same officials, for a country that has joined the Hague Apostille Convention. No authentication above the Secretary of State is needed. |

The country of use determines which of these the office attaches. [source](https://www.sos.mo.gov/Business/Notary/notary/certify) The handbook adds that the apostille must be requested for documents going to member countries. [source](https://www.sos.mo.gov/CMSImages/Business/Notary/NotaryHandbook.pdf) Check your destination in apostille by country, and see apostille versus authentication for what happens after a non-Hague authentication.

## Preparing each document

| Document | What Missouri needs |
| Birth certificate | A certified copy from the Bureau of Vital Records, (573) 751-6387. [source](https://www.sos.mo.gov/Business/Notary/notary/certify) [source](https://health.mo.gov/data/vitalrecords/index.php) |
| Marriage license | A certified copy from the Recorder of Deeds in the county of the marriage, or a statement related to marriage from the Bureau of Vital Records. [source](https://www.sos.mo.gov/Business/Notary/notary/certify) |
| Divorce decree | A certified copy from the Circuit Clerk of the county where the divorce is recorded. [source](https://www.sos.mo.gov/Business/Notary/notary/certify) |
| Diplomas and transcripts | A certified copy from the school. The registrar or another school authority signs a statement typed on the back of the diploma or transcript saying it is the original record (or a copy of it) and the date issued, and a notary witnesses that signature. Don’t alter the face of the diploma. [source](https://www.sos.mo.gov/Business/Notary/notary/certify) [source](https://www.sos.mo.gov/CMSImages/Business/Notary/NotaryHandbook.pdf) |
| Notarized documents | A complete notarization: the notarial paragraph, the notary’s signature, and the seal. [source](https://www.sos.mo.gov/Business/Notary/notary/certify) |

Missouri notaries can’t certify copies of birth certificates, death certificates, divorce decrees, or marriage licenses; those must come certified from the issuing agency. Missouri notaries also can’t certify documents from other states or countries. [source](https://www.sos.mo.gov/CMSImages/Business/Notary/NotaryHandbook.pdf)

## Step by step

- Get the document certified or notarized as shown above. [source](https://www.sos.mo.gov/Business/Notary/notary/certify)
- Fill out the cover letter with your contact details, the number of documents, the country of use, and return instructions. [source](https://www.sos.mo.gov/CMSImages/Business/Notary/CoverLetterComplete.pdf)
- Add payment at $10 per apostille or authentication, or the credit card payment sheet. [source](https://www.sos.mo.gov/CMSImages/Business/Notary/CoverLetterComplete.pdf)
- Plan the return. Documents come back by regular mail unless you include a prepaid envelope with an addressed air bill. If you pay by card and send documents by special delivery, include a completed air bill. [source](https://www.sos.mo.gov/Business/Notary/notary/certify)
The office will also forward documents straight to a third party, such as a consulate, if you enclose a stamped envelope addressed to them. [source](https://www.sos.mo.gov/CMSImages/Business/Notary/NotaryHandbook.pdf)

## Electronic notarizations
Missouri law provides for an electronic certificate of authority for an electronic notarial act, including an electronic form of the apostille, with a fee of up to $10 (section 486.975, reprinted in the Notary Handbook). [source](https://www.sos.mo.gov/CMSImages/Business/Notary/NotaryHandbook.pdf) If you are thinking about notarizing online first, read online notarization for apostille documents, and confirm with the receiving country that it accepts an electronically notarized document.
Rather not do this yourself?
Tell us the document, that it was issued in Missouri, and where it's going. We'll pass your request to an independent apostille service that can handle the whole thing, and they'll reply with a quote. It's free to ask and you're under no obligation.

# How to get an apostille in Pennsylvania
Short answer: The Pennsylvania Department of State’s Office of Notaries, Commissions and Legislation in Harrisburg charges $15 per document (not per page). Walk-in requests at Room 201 of the North Office Building are processed while you wait; by mail, the services page says 5 to 7 business days after receipt, not counting mailing time. [source](https://www.pa.gov/services/dos/get-document-certifications---apostilles)

The Secretary of the Commonwealth authenticates the signatures of Pennsylvania public officials on documents that will be used outside the United States. The destination country decides whether you get an apostille or a certification, and neither is issued for documents used only inside the U.S. [source](https://www.pa.gov/agencies/dos/programs/document-certification)

## At a glance

| Item | What the official page says |
| Fee | $15 per document, not per page. Checks, money orders, or cashier’s checks payable to “Commonwealth of Pennsylvania.” No cash by mail or drop box. [source](https://www.pa.gov/services/dos/get-document-certifications---apostilles) [source](https://www.pa.gov/agencies/dos/programs/document-certification) |
| Walk-in payment | Cash has not been accepted for walk-in service since November 25, 2024. Checks, money orders, and credit cards are accepted, and payment is due when the certification is done. [source](https://www.pa.gov/agencies/dos/programs/document-certification) Credit cards are for walk-in service only. [source](https://www.pa.gov/content/dam/copapwp-pagov/en/dos/programs/document-certification/apostilles-and-authentication.pdf) |
| Walk-in counter | North Office Building, Room 201, 401 North Street, Harrisburg, PA 17120. Monday to Friday, 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., except state holidays; arrive by 4 p.m. The public entrance closes at 3 p.m. daily. [source](https://www.pa.gov/services/dos/get-document-certifications---apostilles) |
| Mailing address | Pennsylvania Department of State, Apostilles & Certifications, North Office Building, Room 201, 401 North Street, Harrisburg, PA 17120-0029 [source](https://www.pa.gov/agencies/dos/programs/document-certification) |
| Mail processing | The services page says 5 to 7 business days after receipt; the program page says to allow about two to three weeks. Neither includes mailing time. [source](https://www.pa.gov/services/dos/get-document-certifications---apostilles) [source](https://www.pa.gov/agencies/dos/programs/document-certification) On its last update (November 19, 2026), the office was processing mail requests received November 16, 2026. [source](https://www.pa.gov/agencies/dos/programs/document-certification) |
| Contact | 717-787-5280, ra-certifications@pa.gov [source](https://www.pa.gov/services/dos/get-document-certifications---apostilles) |

Thanksgiving 2026: the office is closed Thursday and Friday, November 26 and 27, 2026, and recommends arriving no later than 1 p.m. on Wednesday, November 25. [source](https://www.pa.gov/agencies/dos/programs/document-certification)

## Apostille or certification?
For a country that belongs to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention, the department issues an apostille, which needs no further diplomatic or consular legalization. For other countries it attaches a certification, which may still need authentication by the U.S. Department of State and the destination country’s embassy. [source](https://www.pa.gov/agencies/dos/programs/document-certification) Tell the office exactly where the document is going: substituting one for the other delays your documents. [source](https://www.pa.gov/agencies/dos/programs/document-certification)
Pennsylvania now prints both on a single universal certificate, with Spanish and French translations of each section and an electronic seal in black ink instead of a raised gold seal. The department says any certificate can be verified by its certification number in its online document search. [source](https://www.pa.gov/agencies/dos/programs/document-certification) For the general difference, see apostille versus authentication, and check your destination in apostille by country.

## Step by step

- Get an original with the right signature. The document must be an original (no photocopies), signed by and carrying the seal of a Pennsylvania public official: a state elected or appointed official, a county elected official, a judge or magisterial district judge, or a Pennsylvania notary public. [source](https://www.pa.gov/content/dam/copapwp-pagov/en/dos/programs/document-certification/apostilles-and-authentication.pdf) [source](https://www.pa.gov/services/dos/get-document-certifications---apostilles)
- Fill out the request. Use a cover letter or the department’s Request for Legalization of Documents form (also in Chinese and Spanish). Give the destination country and the requester’s name, phone, email, and full mailing address. [source](https://www.pa.gov/services/dos/get-document-certifications---apostilles)
- Pay $15 per document. One check or money order to “Commonwealth of Pennsylvania.” Checks from a foreign bank must be in U.S. dollars and carry a routing number. [source](https://www.pa.gov/services/dos/get-document-certifications---apostilles)
- Add a return envelope. Enclose a self-addressed, stamped envelope, or a prepaid air bill for courier return. For UPS, list yourself as both sender and recipient. FedEx and DHL are not accepted for return shipments. [source](https://www.pa.gov/services/dos/get-document-certifications---apostilles)
- Walk in or mail it. Walk-in customers are served first come, first served; tell the counter how many documents (not pages) and the destination country. [source](https://www.pa.gov/agencies/dos/programs/document-certification)

## Which signature does each document need?

| Document | Pennsylvania rule |
| Birth certificate | Does not need to be, and should not be, notarized. [source](https://www.pa.gov/agencies/dos/programs/document-certification) Birth and death records come from the Pennsylvania Department of Health, Vital Records. [source](https://www.pa.gov/agencies/dos/programs/document-certification) |
| Death certificate | Must be signed by the state registrar. Certificates signed by a local registrar are not accepted. [source](https://www.pa.gov/services/dos/get-document-certifications---apostilles) |
| Marriage certificate | Must be signed by the register of wills or the clerk of the orphans’ court, not only the officiant or clergy. Marriage and divorce records come from the county office where they were filed. [source](https://www.pa.gov/services/dos/get-document-certifications---apostilles) |
| County documents | Must be signed by the clerk in charge of the county office. Documents signed by an assistant or deputy clerk are not accepted. [source](https://www.pa.gov/services/dos/get-document-certifications---apostilles) |
| Diplomas, transcripts, criminal record checks | Must be notarized by a Pennsylvania notary public before you request the apostille or certification. [source](https://www.pa.gov/agencies/dos/programs/document-certification) |
| Notarized documents | The notarial certificate must be worded and completed in English. A version in another language the notary understands may appear immediately next to the English one. [source](https://www.pa.gov/services/dos/get-document-certifications---apostilles) |
| Business documents | Articles of incorporation, certificates of good standing, and bylaws are among the common examples the department authenticates. [source](https://www.pa.gov/services/dos/get-document-certifications---apostilles) |
| FBI checks and other federal documents | Not handled here; the department refers you to the U.S. Department of State. [source](https://www.pa.gov/agencies/dos/programs/document-certification) [source](https://travel.state.gov/content/travel/en/replace-certify-docs/authenticate-your-document/office-of-authentications.html) |

## What gets a request held up?

- Photocopies. Photocopies of notarized or certified documents can’t be certified. [source](https://www.pa.gov/agencies/dos/programs/document-certification)
- The wrong signer. A deputy county clerk, a local registrar on a death certificate, or only the officiant on a marriage certificate. [source](https://www.pa.gov/services/dos/get-document-certifications---apostilles)
- No destination country, or the wrong fee. Both are on the department’s acceptance checklist. [source](https://www.pa.gov/agencies/dos/programs/document-certification)
- Removing the staple. Pennsylvania attaches its certificate only by staple. Don’t remove it after the document is processed. [source](https://www.pa.gov/agencies/dos/programs/document-certification)

## Certificate of Good Standing for a notary
If a Pennsylvania-notarized document is being filed in another state or country that wants proof of the notary’s appointment, the department issues a Certificate of Good Standing for Notary Public. Write a letter asking for one with the notary’s full name and commission ID if known, your name and mailing address, and $15 per certificate. [source](https://www.pa.gov/services/dos/get-document-certifications---apostilles)
Rather not do this yourself?
Tell us the document, that it was issued in Pennsylvania, and where it's going. We'll pass your request to an independent apostille service that can handle the whole thing, and they'll reply with a quote. It's free to ask and you're under no obligation.

- Apostille-USA, true (certified) copy

# How to get an apostille in Washington State
Short answer: The Washington Secretary of State charges $15 per document. Standard mail service typically takes 7 to 10 business days; expedited service adds $100 per 10 documents and typically takes 2 to 3 business days; same-day service in person at Tumwater or Cheney adds $150 for the first 10 documents. [source](https://www.sos.wa.gov/corporations-charities/apostilles-services-information-resource-page) [source](https://www.sos.wa.gov/corporations-charities/frequently-asked-questions-faqs/fee-schedules-priority-services)

The Corporations & Charities Division of the Washington Secretary of State certifies documents signed by a Washington state official or a Washington notary public for use in another country. Washington issues one “universal certificate” that works as an apostille for Hague Convention countries or as an authentication for other countries. [source](https://www.sos.wa.gov/corporations-charities/apostilles-services-information-resource-page)

## Fees and speed

| Service | Fee | Typical time |
| Standard | $15 per document (a document can be more than one page) | 7 to 10 business days from receipt, longer at high volume |
| Expedited | $15 per document, plus $100 per 10 documents (1–10 documents $100, 11–20 documents $200, and so on) | 2 to 3 business days from receipt |
| Same day, in person (Tumwater or Cheney) | $15 per document, plus $150 for the first 10 documents and $100 for each additional 10 (1–10 $150, 11–20 $250, and so on) | Processed while you wait, subject to hours, cutoff times, and volume |

Fees and times as published on the apostille resource page and the fee schedule. [source](https://www.sos.wa.gov/corporations-charities/apostilles-services-information-resource-page) [source](https://www.sos.wa.gov/corporations-charities/frequently-asked-questions-faqs/fee-schedules-priority-services) By mail, pay by check or money order in U.S. dollars to “Secretary of State.” [source](https://www.sos.wa.gov/corporations-charities/apostilles-services-information-resource-page) [source](https://www.sos.wa.gov/sites/default/files/2025-06/6.2025%20-%20Apostilles%20request%20form.pdf) The division says payments are not refundable. [source](https://www.sos.wa.gov/corporations-charities/frequently-asked-questions-faqs/fee-schedules-priority-services)

## Where to go or send it

| Option | Details |
| Mail (USPS) | The division has only one mailing address: PO Box 40234, Olympia, WA 98504-0234. [source](https://www.sos.wa.gov/corporations-charities/contact-us) |
| Overnight courier | UPS, FedEx, and other commercial couriers must use the overnight address, 243 Israel Rd SE, Tumwater, WA 98501, which receives only commercial-carrier overnight deliveries. [source](https://www.sos.wa.gov/corporations-charities/contact-us) |
| In person, Tumwater | 243 Israel Rd SE, Tumwater. Monday to Thursday 8 a.m. to 4 p.m., Friday 8 a.m. to 3 p.m. (Pacific). Documents must be in 30 minutes before closing to make the same-day cutoff. [source](https://www.sos.wa.gov/corporations-charities/contact-us) |
| In person, Cheney | 960 Washington St, Cheney, WA 99004. Monday to Wednesday and Friday, 9 a.m. to 3 p.m. (Pacific); closed Thursdays. Same-day service only, with the $150 same-day fee. This location can’t receive mail. [source](https://www.sos.wa.gov/corporations-charities/contact-us) |
| Phone and chat | 360-725-0377, Monday to Thursday 8 a.m. to 4 p.m., Friday 8 a.m. to 3 p.m. (Pacific) [source](https://www.sos.wa.gov/corporations-charities/contact-us) |

Processed documents go back by regular first-class mail. If your deadline is tight or the documents are going abroad, include a prepaid, traceable return label or envelope. [source](https://www.sos.wa.gov/corporations-charities/apostilles-services-information-resource-page)

## Step by step

- Check the document is eligible. It must be an original or certified copy issued by a Washington government entity, a certified Washington court document, or a personal document notarized by a Washington notary with a full notarial certificate. [source](https://www.sos.wa.gov/corporations-charities/apostilles-services-information-resource-page)
- Fill out the Apostille Authentication Request Form. It asks for the country requesting the document, your name, address, email, and phone, and the number of documents. [source](https://www.sos.wa.gov/sites/default/files/2025-06/6.2025%20-%20Apostilles%20request%20form.pdf)
- Choose standard or expedited and add the fee. [source](https://www.sos.wa.gov/sites/default/files/2025-06/6.2025%20-%20Apostilles%20request%20form.pdf)
- Mail it, courier it, or bring it in using the addresses above. [source](https://www.sos.wa.gov/corporations-charities/contact-us)

## Document rules

| Document | Washington rule |
| Birth, death, marriage, divorce certificates; letter of single status | Send an original certified copy. Vital records must be apostilled by the state that issued them, so a birth certificate from another state goes to that state. [source](https://www.sos.wa.gov/corporations-charities/apostilles-program/apostille-frequently-asked-questions) Certified copies come from the county auditor that issued the marriage certificate or the Center for Vital Statistics in Tumwater. [source](https://www.sos.wa.gov/corporations-charities/apostilles-services-information-resource-page) |
| Public high school transcripts | No notarization, but they must be official transcripts signed by the principal, vice principal, or registrar (a district superintendent or assistant superintendent also works). Ask the school for the signature specifically. [source](https://www.sos.wa.gov/corporations-charities/apostilles-program/apostille-frequently-asked-questions) |
| Washington college and university records | Official transcripts signed by the registrar (associate or interim registrar also accepted); original degrees are signed by the president. Both must carry the school seal. [source](https://www.sos.wa.gov/corporations-charities/apostilles-services-information-resource-page) An original diploma doesn’t need a notary. [source](https://www.sos.wa.gov/corporations-charities/apostilles-program/apostille-frequently-asked-questions) |
| Private and out-of-state school documents | Notarized by a Washington notary. Copies of out-of-state school documents are accepted only when notarized by a Washington notary. [source](https://www.sos.wa.gov/corporations-charities/apostilles-services-information-resource-page) [source](https://www.sos.wa.gov/corporations-charities/apostilles-program/apostille-frequently-asked-questions) |
| Personal documents (power of attorney, affidavits, consents) | Properly notarized by a Washington notary. [source](https://www.sos.wa.gov/corporations-charities/apostilles-services-information-resource-page) |
| Washington background check | A notarized clearance letter from the Washington State Patrol. If the check was fingerprint-based, include the original fingerprint card. [source](https://www.sos.wa.gov/corporations-charities/apostilles-services-information-resource-page) |
| Business entity records | Only certified copies or certificates of documents on file with the Corporations Division. Order the certified copy and the apostille together on the Business Records Request form; these can’t be ordered online. [source](https://www.sos.wa.gov/corporations-charities/apostilles-services-information-resource-page) |
| Driver license or passport | A notarized copy. Outside Washington, you can send an Abstract Driving Record from the Department of Licensing, issued within 30 days of reaching the office. [source](https://www.sos.wa.gov/corporations-charities/apostilles-services-information-resource-page) [source](https://www.sos.wa.gov/corporations-charities/apostilles-program/apostille-frequently-asked-questions) |
| FBI checks, naturalization certificates, military-notary documents | Federal documents; the Secretary of State can’t apostille them. They go to the U.S. Department of State. [source](https://www.sos.wa.gov/corporations-charities/apostilles-services-information-resource-page) [source](https://travel.state.gov/content/travel/en/replace-certify-docs/authenticate-your-document/office-of-authentications.html) |

## What makes a notarization acceptable?
The notary certificate must be complete, signed, and stamped by a Washington notary, with the notary’s signed and printed name, title, commission expiration date, the date of the notarial act, and the Washington state and county where it took place. The signature name and stamp name must match each other and the Notary Division license directory. A notary signature without a notarial certificate can’t be authenticated. [source](https://www.sos.wa.gov/corporations-charities/apostilles-services-information-resource-page)
Since 2016, the Secretary of State won’t certify a notary’s signature on documents about allegiance to a government, renouncing citizenship or military status, or claiming immunity from state or federal law. [source](https://www.sos.wa.gov/corporations-charities/apostilles-services-information-resource-page)

## Non-Hague countries and verification
For a country that isn’t in the Hague Convention, the universal certificate may need further certification by the U.S. Department of State, the country’s embassy, or both. [source](https://www.sos.wa.gov/corporations-charities/apostilles-services-information-resource-page) See apostille versus authentication and apostille by country. The Secretary of State also offers an online apostille and certificate authenticity search. [source](https://www.sos.wa.gov/corporations-charities/apostilles-program/apostille-and-certificate-authenticity-search)
Rather not do this yourself?
Tell us the document, that it was issued in Washington, and where it's going. We'll pass your request to an independent apostille service that can handle the whole thing, and they'll reply with a quote. It's free to ask and you're under no obligation.
Get it done for me
You can also start a request with Apostille-USA. Use the link that matches your document:

- Apostille-USA, original document
- Apostille-USA, true (certified) copy
See the affiliate disclosure for how those links work.

# Apostille Done-Right Checklist Pack
Most apostille rejections come from sending a document to the wrong office or in the wrong form. This pack shows which office handles your document, what it must look like before you send it, and what to put in the envelope, with a cover letter ready to fill in.

## Who it's for

- People sending a birth, marriage or court document abroad
- Businesses sending corporate documents to a foreign bank, registry or partner
- Anyone facing a non-Hague country's embassy legalization for the first time

## How it's sourced
Every fee, address and rule in the pack is cited to the official page: the Hague Conference (HCCH), the U.S. Department of State's Office of Authentications and its fee schedule (22 C.F.R. § 22.1), and each state office named. State office details were checked November 22–23, 2026, the same research behind the state guides on this site.

No. It is general information based on the cited official pages. The receiving country, court or agency decides what it accepts, so confirm with them and check the official office page before you send anything.

### My state isn't in the quick reference. Is the pack still useful?
Yes. The flowchart, document checklists, mailing checklist and letters work for any state. For office details, see our apostille offices by state.

# Apostille by country
The HCCH status table, checked November 23, 2026, lists 130 Contracting Parties to the 1961 Apostille Convention, including the United States. [source](https://www.hcch.net/en/instruments/conventions/status-table/?cid=41) Each country below has its own page with its entry-into-force date, whether the Convention applies with the U.S., and the authority that issues apostilles there.
If the destination country is on this list and the Convention is in force, a U.S. document generally needs an apostille. If it is not on the list, plan on authentication plus embassy or consulate legalization. How the two differ.

## Recent joiners
Countries where the Convention took effect (or takes effect) in 2022 or later. Older guidance may still tell you to get these documents legalized.

- Thailand: takes effect February 28, 2027
- Vietnam: in force since September 11, 2026
- Algeria: in force since July 9, 2026
- Bangladesh: in force since March 30, 2025
- Rwanda: in force since June 5, 2024
- Canada: in force since January 11, 2024
- China: in force since November 7, 2023
- Senegal: in force since March 23, 2023
- Pakistan: in force since March 9, 2023
- Saudi Arabia: in force since December 7, 2022
- Indonesia: in force since June 4, 2022

## Common destinations that are not on the list
These countries and territories did not appear in the HCCH status table on November 23, 2026, so an apostille alone is not the usual route for them: [source](https://www.hcch.net/en/instruments/conventions/status-table/?cid=41)
Afghanistan, Angola, Cambodia, Cameroon, Cuba, Egypt, Ethiopia, Ghana, Haiti, Iran, Iraq, Jordan, Kenya, Kuwait, Lebanon, Libya, Malaysia, Myanmar, Nepal, Nigeria, Qatar, Sri Lanka, Sudan, Syria, Taiwan, Tanzania, Uganda, United Arab Emirates, Yemen, Zambia, Zimbabwe.
For these destinations the chain is usually a state authentication certificate, sometimes a further certificate from the U.S. Department of State, and then legalization by the destination country’s embassy or consulate in the U.S. Each state’s rules differ; see apostille versus authentication and the state offices list.

# How to get an apostille in New Jersey
Short answer: In New Jersey, apostilles come from the Treasury's Division of Revenue and Enterprise Services, not a Secretary of State. Every request starts with a prepaid online order: $25 per document for standard service (12 to 20 business days) or $40 expedited (about 8.5 business hours), plus a card or e-check fee. Then send the original. [source](https://www.njportal.com/dor/apostille) [source](https://www.nj.gov/treasury/revenue/apostilles.shtml)

In New Jersey, apostilles and certifications come from the Department of the Treasury, Division of Revenue and Enterprise Services, not from a Secretary of State. Every request starts with an online order that you prepay, and you then mail or hand-deliver the original document with the printed order confirmation. [source](https://www.nj.gov/treasury/revenue/apostilles.shtml) [source](https://www.njportal.com/dor/apostille)

## At a glance

| Item | What the official page says |
| Issuing office | New Jersey Department of the Treasury, Division of Revenue and Enterprise Services. Apostilles and certifications are one-page, 8.5 x 11 documents with a color print of the Great Seal of the State of New Jersey and the signature of the State Treasurer, stapled to the signature page of your document. Do not remove it. [source](https://www.nj.gov/treasury/revenue/apostilles.shtml) |
| Standard fee | $25.00 per record (non-adoption), plus a $2.50 credit card or $1.00 e-check service fee. Adoption documents: $5.00 per document, no service fee. [source](https://www.njportal.com/dor/apostille) |
| Expedited fee | $40.00 per document (non-adoption), plus the same card or e-check service fee. Adoption documents: $20.00 per document. [source](https://www.njportal.com/dor/apostille) |
| Standard processing | 12 to 20 business days from the date the document is received and entered in the system. [source](https://www.njportal.com/dor/apostille) |
| Expedited processing | 8.5 business hours from the time the document is received and entered in the system, subject to daily workload. [source](https://www.njportal.com/dor/apostille) |
| Faster options | Accelerated processing of 1 or 2 business hours is available at “substantially higher fees.” For that service, call 609-292-9292. [source](https://www.njportal.com/dor/apostille) |
| Payment | Online only, by e-check (debit) or credit card, when you place the order. [source](https://www.njportal.com/dor/apostille) |

## Step by step

- Get the right original. You need the original or a certified copy of the document that carries the original notarization or the original certification of the public official. [source](https://www.nj.gov/treasury/revenue/apostilles.shtml)
- Check the notarization. A notarized document must carry the original (inked) signature of the New Jersey notary public and the original (inked) signature of the person who presented the document for notarization. [source](https://www.nj.gov/treasury/revenue/apostilles.shtml)
- Place the online order. The order asks for your contact details, a description of each document (for example the state registrar, the notary’s commission ID, and the date of the event), the processing level, how you want the documents returned, and payment. [source](https://www.njportal.com/dor/apostille) You must place a separate online order for each country where you will present the documents. [source](https://www.njportal.com/dor/apostille)
- Send the original with the confirmation. Print the order confirmation that is emailed to you and send it with the original documents, as described below. [source](https://www.njportal.com/dor/apostille)

## Where do you send the document?

| Service | How to deliver |
| Standard (by mail) | Mail the originals and the printed confirmation by USPS first class, Priority, or Certified Mail to Division of Revenue and Enterprise Services, PO Box 452, Trenton, NJ 08646. [source](https://www.njportal.com/dor/apostille) |
| Expedited (in person) | Customer Service Counter, 33 West State Street, 5th floor, Trenton, NJ 08608, between 8:30 a.m. and 2:00 p.m. If you deliver in person, you can wait for the apostille; the wait can be up to 2.5 hours, and walk-in service depends on workload, so the office suggests calling 609-292-9292 before you go. [source](https://www.njportal.com/dor/apostille) |
| Expedited (courier) | Send it by an express delivery service such as UPS or FedEx to the same 33 West State Street address. The US Postal Service is not available for expedited requests. [source](https://www.njportal.com/dor/apostille) |

## Which documents will New Jersey certify?
The Division certifies the signatures of New Jersey notaries public and selected public officials, such as Superior Court judges, county clerks, and the State Registrar of Vital Statistics. [source](https://www.nj.gov/treasury/revenue/apostilles.shtml)
It issues an apostille when the document is going to a country that belongs to the Hague Convention. For a country that is not on the Hague list, it issues a certification of the public official instead. See apostille versus authentication. [source](https://www.nj.gov/treasury/revenue/apostilles.shtml)

### Birth, marriage, and other vital records
Vital records (birth, marriage, divorce, death, and so on) from January 1, 1923 forward come from the New Jersey Department of Health, Office of Vital Statistics and Registry (609-292-4087). For records dated before January 1, 1923, contact the New Jersey State Archives. [source](https://www.nj.gov/treasury/revenue/apostilles.shtml)
New Jersey cannot issue apostilles or certifications for vital records from other states. Those must be authenticated in the state where they were issued. [source](https://www.nj.gov/treasury/revenue/apostilles.shtml)

### Documents in another language
For documents that are not in English, the Division recommends attaching a notarized English translation. If you attach a notarized translation to a vital record, it issues two apostilles or certifications and charges two fees. [source](https://www.nj.gov/treasury/revenue/apostilles.shtml)
Rather not do this yourself?
Tell us the document, that it was issued in New Jersey, and where it's going. We'll pass your request to an independent apostille service that can handle the whole thing, and they'll reply with a quote. It's free to ask and you're under no obligation.
Get it done for me
You can also start a request with Apostille-USA. Use the link that matches your document:

- Apostille-USA, original document
- Apostille-USA, true (certified) copy
See the affiliate disclosure for how those links work.

- New York apostille: if your document was notarized or issued across the river, it goes to New York, not Trenton.
- Pennsylvania apostille: documents issued or notarized in Pennsylvania go to Harrisburg.

# How to get an apostille in North Carolina
Short answer: The North Carolina Secretary of State's Authentication Office in Raleigh charges $10 per document and issues an Apostille, an Authentication or an Authority certificate, depending on the country and the document. There is no online filing. Walk in at 2 South Salisbury Street with no appointment, or mail it; mail generally takes five business days longer. [source](https://www.sosnc.gov/fees/by_title/_authentications) [source](https://www.sosnc.gov/divisions/authentications/Apostille_Certificates) [source](https://www.sosnc.gov/divisions/authentications/TurnAround_Times)

The North Carolina Secretary of State’s Authentication Office in Raleigh issues apostilles, authentications, and certificates for North Carolina documents, including birth and marriage certificates, statements of marital status, corporate documents, powers of attorney, diplomas, school transcripts, and deeds. [source](https://www.sosnc.gov/divisions/authentications)

## At a glance

| Item | What the official page says |
| Fee | $10.00 per document. For adoptions, a duplicate original requested at the same time is $5.00; requested later, $10.00. Checks or money orders payable to “North Carolina Secretary of State.” [source](https://www.sosnc.gov/fees/by_title/_authentications) [source](https://www.sosnc.gov/divisions/authentications/Apostille_Certificates) |
| Refunds | The $10 fee may be refunded if the document is rejected, not processed, and you request a refund. [source](https://www.sosnc.gov/divisions/authentications/Apostille_Certificates) |
| Mailing address | North Carolina Secretary of State, Authentication Office, Post Office Box 29622, Raleigh, North Carolina 27626-0622 [source](https://www.sosnc.gov/divisions/authentications) |
| Walk-in address | North Carolina Secretary of State, Authentication Office, 2 South Salisbury Street, Raleigh, North Carolina 27601-2903. Phone 919-814-5400. Office hours Monday to Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. [source](https://www.sosnc.gov/divisions/authentications) |
| In person | No appointment needed. Hand-delivered documents are generally processed more quickly than mailed ones. [source](https://www.sosnc.gov/divisions/authentications/TurnAround_Times) |
| Mail processing | Mailed documents generally take five business days longer than hand-delivered documents. The office posts current turnaround times on its authentications home page. [source](https://www.sosnc.gov/divisions/authentications/TurnAround_Times) |
| Online filing | None. The office says it does not do online authentications. [source](https://www.sosnc.gov/frequently_asked_questions/by_title/_Authentications) |

## Which certificate do you need?
North Carolina issues three different certificates, and which one you get depends on the destination country and the kind of document: [source](https://www.sosnc.gov/frequently_asked_questions/by_title/_Authentications)

| Certificate | Used for |
| Apostille | Documents going to countries that have signed the Hague Convention. |
| Authentication | North Carolina government-issued documents going to countries that have not signed the Hague Convention. |
| Authority | Documents notarized in North Carolina going to countries that have not signed the Hague Convention. |

Once you have an apostille, the document can go directly to the destination country without further certification from the U.S. Department of State. [source](https://www.sosnc.gov/divisions/authentications/Apostille_Certificates) For how the two systems differ, see apostille versus authentication.

## Step by step

- Make sure it is in English. If the document is in another language, get a certified or notarized English translation. [source](https://www.sosnc.gov/divisions/authentications/Apostille_Certificates) Since late 2024, the English translation must carry a wet (original) signature. [source](https://www.sosnc.gov/frequently_asked_questions/by_title/_Authentications)
- Get the right signature on it. Sign before a North Carolina notary, or get a certified copy notarized by the issuing entity. For a copy of a North Carolina document, you can use a notarized “true copy” affidavit; the office provides a sample on its cover letters and templates page. [source](https://www.sosnc.gov/divisions/authentications/Apostille_Certificates)
- Prepare the cover letter. It needs a contact name, a daytime phone number, the country where the document will be used, and the correct fee. [source](https://www.sosnc.gov/frequently_asked_questions/by_title/_Authentications) The cover letter is on the office’s forms page. [source](https://www.sosnc.gov/forms/by_title/_Authentications)
- Send or deliver it. Include the original documents with all certifications attached, the payment, and a prepaid return envelope or carrier label. [source](https://www.sosnc.gov/divisions/authentications/Apostille_Certificates)

## Which documents don’t need a notary?
Documents from these North Carolina offices go straight to the Authentication Office without a notarization: [source](https://www.sosnc.gov/divisions/authentications/Apostille_Certificates)

- Register of Deeds
- Clerk of Superior Court
- North Carolina Department of Agriculture
- North Carolina Department of Health and Human Services
- North Carolina Vital Records (phone 919-733-3526)
- North Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (Raleigh office only)
- North Carolina Attorney General’s Office
- North Carolina Legislative Services

## Diplomas and transcripts
Transcripts, report cards, diplomas, and similar documents from a North Carolina university, college, community college, or high school must be notarized by a North Carolina notary public. A school seal applied by the registrar is not acceptable. [source](https://www.sosnc.gov/divisions/authentications/Apostille_Certificates)

## What gets a request rejected?

- Old signatures. The certifying official’s signature must be from April 2000 or later, because the office does not have official signatures on record from before 2000. [source](https://www.sosnc.gov/frequently_asked_questions/by_title/_Authentications) [source](https://www.sosnc.gov/divisions/authentications/Apostille_Certificates)
- Out-of-state documents. North Carolina can’t authenticate a document from another state. [source](https://www.sosnc.gov/frequently_asked_questions/by_title/_Authentications)
- Missing translation. A foreign-language document without a certified or notarized English translation is denied. [source](https://www.sosnc.gov/frequently_asked_questions/by_title/_Authentications)
- U.S. use. Documents to be used in the United States can’t be authenticated. [source](https://www.sosnc.gov/frequently_asked_questions/by_title/_Authentications)

## Return shipping
Without a prepaid label or self-addressed stamped envelope, documents come back by regular mail. A prepaid courier label must be computer-printed and paid for when you print it; a handwritten label with an account number doesn’t count. The office rejects FedEx labels that list the Secretary of State with “Bill Sender.” UPS and FedEx air labels are picked up automatically; for ground labels, the office calls you and you schedule the pickup. [source](https://www.sosnc.gov/divisions/authentications/Courier_Policies) [source](https://www.sosnc.gov/divisions/authentications/Apostille_Certificates)
For documents going back to a foreign address, the office no longer uses UPS, FedEx, or DHL. It will mail a USPS prepaid envelope and label to a foreign address as long as the sender address isn’t the Secretary of State’s. [source](https://www.sosnc.gov/divisions/authentications/Courier_Policies)
Emergencies can be considered for expedited processing if you send documentation of the emergency. [source](https://www.sosnc.gov/divisions/authentications/Apostille_Certificates)
Rather not do this yourself?
Tell us the document, that it was issued in North Carolina, and where it's going. We'll pass your request to an independent apostille service that can handle the whole thing, and they'll reply with a quote. It's free to ask and you're under no obligation.
Get it done for me
You can also start a request with Apostille-USA. Use the link that matches your document:

- Apostille-USA, original document
- Apostille-USA, true (certified) copy
See the affiliate disclosure for how those links work.

# How to get an apostille in Virginia
Short answer: Virginia's Secretary of the Commonwealth issues an Apostille or Great Seal authentication for $10 per document, or $5 for each extra document signed by the same official on the same date for the same country. Every request needs an online cover letter. Mail generally takes 7 to 10 business days; in-person service is by appointment only. [source](https://www.commonwealth.virginia.gov/official-documents/authentications/how-to-submit/) [source](https://www.commonwealth.virginia.gov/official-documents/authentications/)

The Office of the Secretary of the Commonwealth, Authentication Division, issues Virginia’s authentications. Depending on the destination country, the certificate is either an Apostille or a Great Seal authentication. It confirms that the Virginia notary, Virginia clerk of court, or Virginia deputy state registrar is in the office’s system and notarized or issued your document correctly. [source](https://www.commonwealth.virginia.gov/official-documents/authentications/)
Two Virginia rules catch people out. Notarized documents, vital records, court records, and State Corporation Commission documents must all be dated within the past 12 months. And Virginia cannot currently authenticate a document signed by a Virginia electronic notary (eNotary). [source](https://www.commonwealth.virginia.gov/official-documents/authentications/types-of-documents/)

## At a glance

| Item | What the official page says |
| Fee | $10.00 per document, not per page. If several documents were signed by the same public official on the same date for the same country, it is $10.00 for the first and $5.00 for each additional document. Checks and money orders payable to the Secretary of the Commonwealth. Overpayments of $5 or less may not be refunded. [source](https://www.commonwealth.virginia.gov/official-documents/authentications/how-to-submit/) |
| Cover letter | Required with every request. You create it online on the state’s authentications cover-letter site, which requires you to register or log in. [source](https://www.commonwealth.virginia.gov/official-documents/authentications/how-to-submit/) |
| Mail processing | Generally 7 to 10 business days from when you send the documents. You can ask about status only after 7 to 10 days have passed. [source](https://www.commonwealth.virginia.gov/official-documents/authentications/how-to-submit/) On November 23, 2026, the office’s main page carried a holiday notice that processing and return shipping for authentication requests was running about 4 weeks. [source](https://www.commonwealth.virginia.gov/official-documents/authentications/) |
| In person | By appointment only, Monday through Thursday, up to 10 documents. Most authentications are processed the same day if the documents are properly notarized or issued. Without an appointment you will not be seen. [source](https://www.commonwealth.virginia.gov/official-documents/authentications/how-to-submit/) |
| Drop box | Without an appointment, you can leave documents in the drop box at 400 East Cary Street. They are processed and returned in your prepaid mailer within 5 to 7 business days. [source](https://www.commonwealth.virginia.gov/official-documents/authentications/how-to-submit/) |
| Phone and email | 804-692-0114, notary@governor.virginia.gov [source](https://www.commonwealth.virginia.gov/official-documents/authentications/) |

## Addresses: USPS and couriers go to different places

| How you send it | Address |
| U.S. Postal Service | Office of the Secretary of the Commonwealth, Authentication Division, 1111 East Broad Street, Richmond, Virginia 23219 [source](https://www.commonwealth.virginia.gov/official-documents/authentications/) |
| FedEx, UPS, or DHL | Office of the Secretary of the Commonwealth, Authentication Division, 400 East Cary Street, Richmond, Virginia 23219 [source](https://www.commonwealth.virginia.gov/official-documents/authentications/) |
| Appointments and drop box | 400 East Cary Street, Richmond, VA 23219, behind the Virginia Department of Health. Limited public parking and street parking. [source](https://www.commonwealth.virginia.gov/official-documents/authentications/how-to-submit/) |

Include the cover letter, payment, and a self-addressed, prepaid return mailer. For FedEx, UPS, or DHL return labels, list your own name and address as both sender and recipient. If the office is listed as the sender, your documents come back by regular mail without tracking. [source](https://www.commonwealth.virginia.gov/official-documents/authentications/how-to-submit/)

## Booking an appointment
Appointments open online only on Fridays at 10:00 a.m., for the following week only. The limit is 10 documents per customer or family, and one appointment per family member per day. Bring a valid government-issued ID (required for all adults entering the building), limit your party to two people, and print or photograph your appointment confirmation. [source](https://www.commonwealth.virginia.gov/official-documents/authentications/how-to-submit/)
Appointments are for individual constituents. Couriers and apostille companies must use the drop box, and those documents are returned by mail only. [source](https://www.commonwealth.virginia.gov/official-documents/authentications/how-to-submit/)

## What will Virginia authenticate?

| Document | Requirement |
| Notarized document | Properly notarized by a Virginia notary within the past 12 months. Virginia does not accept documents notarized in another state. [source](https://www.commonwealth.virginia.gov/official-documents/authentications/types-of-documents/) |
| Birth, death, marriage, or divorce certificate | Must be issued by the Virginia Department of Health, Vital Records (or your local DMV) within the past 12 months, and must not be notarized. Circuit Court marriage certificates need a Certification of Official Record (triple seal). [source](https://www.commonwealth.virginia.gov/official-documents/authentications/types-of-documents/) |
| Court record | Issued by the Virginia Circuit Court within the past 12 months with a Certification of Official Record (triple seal), showing the date and the clerk’s signature and printed name. Cannot be notarized. [source](https://www.commonwealth.virginia.gov/official-documents/authentications/types-of-documents/) |
| Business documents | A State Corporation Commission document issued within the past 12 months and signed by the Clerk of the Commission. To order one, call the SCC at 804-371-9733 and ask for a certified copy for international authentication. [source](https://www.commonwealth.virginia.gov/official-documents/authentications/types-of-documents/) |

Virginia will not process federal documents, including FBI background checks, or documents notarized by military notaries. Those go to the U.S. Department of State’s Office of Authentications. It also will not process out-of-state documents, including out-of-state school transcripts and diplomas. [source](https://www.commonwealth.virginia.gov/official-documents/authentications/types-of-documents/)
Virginia does not require a translation before you submit, but the notarization itself must be in English. [source](https://www.commonwealth.virginia.gov/official-documents/authentications/) [source](https://www.commonwealth.virginia.gov/official-documents/authentications/types-of-documents/)

## What does a Virginia notarization need?
The office rejects a notarized document unless it shows all of these: [source](https://www.commonwealth.virginia.gov/official-documents/authentications/types-of-documents/)

- the county or independent city where the document was signed;
- the date of notarization;
- the notarial statement saying what is being notarized (a signature, a true copy of an original, or an oath);
- the notary’s signature;
- the notary’s commission expiration date (month, day, year);
- the notary’s registration number;
- a photographically reproducible seal or stamp with the name matching the office’s records exactly.
Other common rejection reasons include a notarization more than 12 months old, a notarization split across pages, and a photocopy of a notarization. [source](https://www.commonwealth.virginia.gov/official-documents/authentications/document-rejection/)

## Can Virginia apostille an electronic notarization?
The Virginia authentications page says that, at this time, it cannot authenticate an electronic notarization with an Apostille or Great Seal authentication. [source](https://www.commonwealth.virginia.gov/official-documents/authentications/types-of-documents/) If your document is headed abroad from Virginia, have it notarized in person by a commissioned Virginia notary. The office says many banks, FedEx stores, UPS stores, and USPS locations offer notary services. Other states handle this differently; see online notarization for apostille documents. [source](https://www.commonwealth.virginia.gov/official-documents/authentications/)
Rather not do this yourself?
Tell us the document, that it was issued in Virginia, and where it's going. We'll pass your request to an independent apostille service that can handle the whole thing, and they'll reply with a quote. It's free to ask and you're under no obligation.

# Online notarization for apostille documents
Short answer: Often, yes, but the online notary doesn't issue the apostille. You still send the notarized original to the state office for the notary's state. Texas apostilles remote online notarizations if you include the notary's ledger details, Virginia can't apostille electronic notarizations, and some countries refuse remotely notarized documents even after authentication. [source](https://www.sos.texas.gov/authinfo.shtml) [source](https://www.commonwealth.virginia.gov/official-documents/authentications/types-of-documents/)

A remote online notary (RON) can notarize a document over two-way audio and video. The apostille, if you need one, still comes from the competent authority in the state of the notary or the record, not from the notarization platform.
This page covers only what official government pages said when we checked them on November 22, 2026. An online notary platform does not issue an apostille. Some destination countries refuse remotely notarized documents even after a state office authenticates them.

## Does an online notary issue the apostille?
Notarization confirms that a signer appeared before a notary and that the notarial certificate was completed. An apostille authenticates the notary’s (or other public official’s) signature, seal, and capacity for use abroad. California’s official FAQ puts it this way: an apostille certifies the authenticity of the public official’s signature, the capacity in which that official acted, and, when appropriate, the identity of the seal or stamp; it “does not validate the contents of the document.” [source](https://www.sos.ca.gov/notary/apostille-faqs)
If the document is a notarized private paper (for example, a power of attorney or a school-record affidavit), you typically get it notarized first, then send the original notarized document to the state office. If it is a vital record or court paper, you usually need a certified copy from the issuing agency, not a fresh notarization.

## What official pages say, state by state

### Texas
The Texas Secretary of State is explicit. “Online (RON) notarization documents can be apostilled by our Office if presented with the following items:” a notarization ledger that details the date and time signatures were applied, a document description, and signer information; and “a true and accurate notarial certificate, which contains the required statements indicating the document was notarized via ‘electronic or online notarization by two-way audio and visual communication.’” [source](https://www.sos.texas.gov/authinfo.shtml)
The same official page warns: “some countries do not accept online (RON) notarized documents, even if properly authenticated by our Office. Please verify with the agency, or entity you are submitting your documents to in order to ensure they accept this type of notarization.” [source](https://www.sos.texas.gov/authinfo.shtml)
Texas also requires that documents be “issued from the state of Texas or properly notarized by a Texas notary” to qualify for an apostille. [source](https://www.sos.texas.gov/statdoc/request.shtml)

### Florida
Florida has authorized remote online notarization since January 1, 2020, under Chapter 2019-71, Laws of Florida, and Rule 1N-7.001 of the Florida Administrative Code. Only an already commissioned Florida notary (or a qualifying civil-law notary or commissioner of deeds) may register as an online notary, after training, an application, and an initial $10 fee. [source](https://dos.fl.gov/sunbiz/other-services/notaries/remote-online-notary-public)
The Florida apostille page lists “Documents Notarized by a Florida Notary Public” among the documents the Division of Corporations will authenticate. [source](https://dos.fl.gov/sunbiz/other-services/apostille-notarial-certification) That page does not publish a separate RON checklist (for example, it does not mention a ledger). If you have a remotely notarized Florida document, confirm the current attachment requirements with the Apostille Section before you mail it.

### New York
New York’s notary FAQ discusses electronic notarization, including fees: “An Electronic Notary may charge up to $25.00 per electronic notarial act performed,” and “A certificate of authenticity for any document that has been created through an electronic notarial act is a notarial act for which $2.00 may be charged.” [source](https://dos.ny.gov/notary-public-frequently-asked-questions) Those are notary fees, not the Department of State apostille fee.
The official apostille page requires notarized documents to be certified by the county clerk of the county where the notary is commissioned, then submitted to the Department of State with a $10 fee per document. [source](https://dos.ny.gov/apostille-certificate-authentication) That page, checked November 22, 2026, does not specifically describe remote or electronic notarizations. Confirm with the Apostille and Authentication Unit, and with the county clerk, before you rely on a RON document.

### Virginia
Virginia says plainly that, at this time, it cannot authenticate an electronic notarization with an Apostille or Great Seal authentication. A Virginia document headed abroad needs an in-person notarization by a Virginia notary, within the past 12 months. [source](https://www.commonwealth.virginia.gov/official-documents/authentications/types-of-documents/) See the Virginia apostille guide.

### California and Massachusetts
The California request-an-apostille and apostille FAQ pages, and the Massachusetts apostilles page, checked November 22, 2026, do not address remote online notarization. California will apostille a document signed by a California public official or “an original notarized and/or certified document.” [source](https://www.sos.ca.gov/notary/request-apostille) Massachusetts will certify documents that carry an original signature of a valid Massachusetts notary public (or certain other named officials), and says photocopied signatures can’t be certified. [source](https://www.sec.state.ma.us/divisions/commissions/apostilles.htm) Whether a particular electronically notarized document meets those offices’ current requirements is not stated on those pages, so ask the office before you file.

## Online notarization platforms
These companies provide online notarization. They are not government offices and they do not issue apostilles. Compare their current prices and state coverage on their own sites, and confirm that the notary is commissioned in the same state as the office that will apostille the document.

- Notarize (Proof)
- BlueNotary
- OneNotary
- NotaryLive

# Apostille offices by state
An apostille for a state document comes from that state, not from the federal government. The U.S. designation on file with the Hague Conference names the officers in each state, D.C., and several territories who can sign one. [source](https://www.hcch.net/en/states/authorities/details3/?aid=353) In most states that is the Secretary of State; a few use the Lieutenant Governor, the Secretary of the Commonwealth, or another office.
Federal documents go to the U.S. Department of State Office of Authentications instead, and U.S. federal court documents to the clerk of that court. [source](https://www.hcch.net/en/states/authorities/details3/?aid=353) If you'd rather have a service handle a federal (U.S. Department of State) apostille, one option is Apostille-USA. For where your document is headed, see apostille by country.

| State or territory | Apostille authority | Officers designated to sign | Verify an apostille online |
| Alabama | Secretary of State | Secretary of State | — |
| Alaska | Lieutenant Governor | Lieutenant Governor; Attorney General and Clerk of the Appellate Courts | — |
| Arizona | Secretary of State | Secretary of State; Assistant Secretary of State | — |
| Arkansas | Secretary of State | Secretary of State; Chief Deputy Secretary of State | — |
| California | Secretary of State | Secretary of State; any Assistant Secretary of State; any Deputy Secretary of State | Search |
| Colorado | Secretary of State | Secretary of State; Deputy Secretary of State | Search |

| Rhode Island | Secretary of State | Secretary of State; First Deputy Secretary of State; Second Deputy Secretary of State | Search |
| South Carolina | Secretary of State | Secretary of State | — |

## Checking that an apostille is genuine
The Apostille Convention lets each competent authority keep a register of the apostilles it issues. 12 of the jurisdictions above publish an online search: California, Colorado, Connecticut, Delaware, Kentucky, New York, Rhode Island, Tennessee, Texas, Utah, Washington, West Virginia. For the others, contact the issuing office. Our guide to verifying an apostille has the full list of U.S. e-Registers from the Hague Conference’s November 2026 chart and the steps to follow.
