# How to get an apostille in California
Short answer: The California Secretary of State charges $20 per apostille. In person in Sacramento or Los Angeles, add a $6 special handling fee per official's signature; most requests are done within about 30 minutes. Mailed requests go only to Sacramento, are handled in the order received and can't be expedited, so check the posted processing date first. [source](https://www.sos.ca.gov/notary/request-apostille) [source](https://www.sos.ca.gov/notary/processing-times)

The California Secretary of State issues an apostille that authenticates a California public official’s signature on a document to be used outside the United States. The office issues a single apostille regardless of the destination country; it does not issue a separate authentication certificate.

## At a glance

| Item | What the official page says |
| Issuing office | California Secretary of State, Notary Public Section [source](https://www.sos.ca.gov/notary/request-apostille) |
| Fee by mail | $20.00 per apostille. Check or money order payable to Secretary of State. The $6 special handling fee does not apply to mail. [source](https://www.sos.ca.gov/notary/request-apostille) |
| Fee in person | $20.00 per apostille plus a $6.00 special handling fee for each different public official’s signature being authenticated. [source](https://www.sos.ca.gov/notary/apostille-faqs) |
| Mail | Yes, processed only by the Sacramento office, in the order received. Same-day or pulled expedited service is not offered for mail. |
| Mailing addresses | USPS: Notary Public Section, P.O. Box 942877, Sacramento, CA 94277-0001. FedEx, UPS, DHL, and similar: Notary Public Section, 1500 11th Street, 2nd Floor, Sacramento, CA 95814. [source](https://www.sos.ca.gov/notary/request-apostille) |
| In person | Same-day service at the Sacramento 3rd-floor public counter (1500 11th Street, 3rd Floor, Sacramento, CA 95814) and at the Los Angeles office in the Ronald Reagan building, 300 South Spring Street, Room 12513, Los Angeles, CA 90013 (no appointments). Arrive by 4:30 p.m. to guarantee service. [source](https://www.sos.ca.gov/notary/request-apostille) [source](https://www.sos.ca.gov/notary/processing-times) |
| Processing as published | In person: typically within 30 minutes after submission. Mail: as of November 20, 2026, Sacramento was processing apostille requests received November 12, 2026. [source](https://www.sos.ca.gov/notary/processing-times) |

## What do you include in a mailed request?
Four items are required for a mail request: [source](https://www.sos.ca.gov/notary/request-apostille)

- The document that needs the apostille. It must be signed by a California public official, or be an original notarized and/or certified document. A photocopy is not acceptable.
- A cover sheet stating the country in which the document will be used (the office’s mail cover sheet, or your own).
- A check or money order payable to Secretary of State for $20.00 per apostille.
- A self-addressed envelope for return. Provide prepaid postage if you want a tracked service; otherwise the office returns the document by regular U.S. mail.
Anyone may request an apostille in person, including on behalf of someone else, and the requester does not need to be related to a person named in the document. [source](https://www.sos.ca.gov/notary/apostille-faqs)
Payment in Sacramento may be by credit card (Visa or Mastercard), check, money order, or cash. The Los Angeles office accepts credit card (Visa or Mastercard), check, or money order; cash is not accepted there. [source](https://www.sos.ca.gov/notary/request-apostille)

## In-person special handling examples
The official FAQ gives these totals for in-person requests, combining the $20 apostille fee with the $6 special handling fee that applies once per distinct public official’s signature: [source](https://www.sos.ca.gov/notary/apostille-faqs)

| Example | Total |
| 1 document, 1 public official | $26.00 |
| 2 documents, 1 public official | $46.00 |
| 2 documents, 2 public officials | $52.00 |
| 5 documents, 1 public official | $106.00 |
| 5 documents, 5 public officials | $130.00 |

## Vital records
For California birth and death certificates, the Secretary of State can issue an apostille for the signatures of county clerks and their deputies, county recorders and their deputies, and the State Registrar at the California Department of Public Health. If a city- or county-level certificate is signed by a health officer or county registrar, the official FAQ says you may first need a county-clerk certification or a certified copy from the county recorder or the state Department of Public Health. [source](https://www.sos.ca.gov/notary/apostille-faqs)

## Office notes when we checked
The processing-dates page, last updated November 20, 2026, said the Los Angeles office was temporarily providing services on the 1st floor in suite 1215 because of an elevator outage. Confirm that note on the official page before you go. [source](https://www.sos.ca.gov/notary/processing-times)
The Secretary of State also holds periodic in-person apostille pop-up shops around the state; dates are listed on the request page. [source](https://www.sos.ca.gov/notary/request-apostille)
Rather not do this yourself?
Tell us the document, that it was issued in California, and where it's going. We'll pass your request to an independent apostille service that can handle the whole thing, and they'll reply with a quote. It's free to ask and you're under no obligation.

# How to get an apostille in Florida
Short answer: Only the Florida Department of State's Division of Corporations in Tallahassee issues apostilles: $10 per document, or $20 for documents certified by a county clerk of court. Pay by check or money order; cash and cards aren't accepted. Walk-in requests are usually finished while you wait, and mail is processed in the order received. [source](https://dos.fl.gov/sunbiz/other-services/apostille-notarial-certification)

The Florida Secretary of State is the only competent authority authorized to issue notarial and apostille certifications in Florida. The Division of Corporations issues them from its Tallahassee office.

## At a glance

| Item | What the official page says |
| Issuing office | Florida Department of State, Division of Corporations, Apostille Section, The Centre of Tallahassee, 2415 N. Monroe Street, Suite 810, Tallahassee, FL 32303 [source](https://dos.fl.gov/sunbiz/other-services/apostille-notarial-certification) |
| Fee | $10.00 per document; or $20.00 per document for documents certified by any Florida county clerk of court when you are requesting an apostille ($10 for the apostille and $10 for a certificate of incumbency). [source](https://dos.fl.gov/sunbiz/other-services/apostille-notarial-certification) |
| Payment | Check or money order payable to the Florida Department of State, in U.S. currency drawn from a U.S. bank. Cash and credit cards are not accepted. [source](https://dos.fl.gov/sunbiz/other-services/apostille-notarial-certification) |
| Mail | Yes. Include the official request form, the document, payment, and a self-addressed stamped envelope or a prepaid, pre-addressed air bill with the requestor’s name and address as both sender and recipient. |
| Mailing addresses | Mail: Department of State, Division of Corporations, Apostilles Section, P.O. Box 6800, Tallahassee, FL 32314 (the official request form prints the ZIP as 32314-6800). Courier or physical: 2415 N. Monroe Street, Suite 810, Tallahassee, FL 32303. [source](https://dos.fl.gov/sunbiz/contact/address-phone-numbers/) [source](https://dos.fl.gov/media/702388/1-apostille_and_notarial_certificate_request_form-10-19-2023.pdf) |
| In person | Walk-in service at 2415 N. Monroe Street, Suite 810, Tallahassee, Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., except state holidays. “Most requests may be completed while you wait.” The office does not offer expedited service. [source](https://dos.fl.gov/sunbiz/other-services/apostille-notarial-certification/faq) |
| Processing as published | Documents are processed in the order received. The document-processing-dates page, updated November 20, 2026, listed apostille requests as currently processing documents received November 16, 2026. [source](https://dos.fl.gov/sunbiz/document-processing-dates) |

## How do you file for a Florida apostille?
The official “How to File” steps are: [source](https://dos.fl.gov/sunbiz/other-services/apostille-notarial-certification)

- Complete the Department of State’s Apostille and Notarial Certificate Request Form.
- Enclose the document. An original certified copy or certificate of status of a public document is required; a photocopy is not acceptable. Notarized documents must contain a full notarial statement and the original notary’s signature, stamp, and seal.
- Insert a self-addressed stamped envelope, or a prepaid, pre-addressed air bill, with the requestor listed as both sender and recipient.
- Include payment.
- Mail the packet to the Apostille Section.

## Do you need an apostille or a notarial certification?
An apostille is issued for use in a country that is a member of the 1961 Hague Convention. “Countries that are nonmembers of the 1961 Hague Convention are not issued an apostille; they are issued notarial certificates or certifications.” Both certificates authenticate the issuing official’s or notary’s signature. [source](https://dos.fl.gov/sunbiz/other-services/apostille-notarial-certification/faq)

## Which documents will Florida authenticate?
The official page lists, among others: Florida agency or official documents; Florida birth and death certificates; circuit court and clerk-of-the-county documents; marriage and divorce certificates; school transcripts; vehicle titles; documents notarized by a Florida notary public; Florida criminal background checks from the Florida Department of Law Enforcement or local law enforcement; and Secretary of State certified copies and certificates of status. [source](https://dos.fl.gov/sunbiz/other-services/apostille-notarial-certification)
Federal documents should be submitted to the U.S. Department of State. A document issued or notarized in another state should go to that state’s competent authority. [source](https://dos.fl.gov/sunbiz/other-services/apostille-notarial-certification)
The office does not translate documents. It also states that the person who translates a document cannot be the person who notarizes it. [source](https://dos.fl.gov/sunbiz/other-services/apostille-notarial-certification/faq)
Rather not do this yourself?
Tell us the document, that it was issued in Florida, and where it's going. We'll pass your request to an independent apostille service that can handle the whole thing, and they'll reply with a quote. It's free to ask and you're under no obligation.

# How to get an apostille in Massachusetts
Short answer: Massachusetts apostilles come from the Secretary of the Commonwealth's Commissions Section and cost $6 per document, paid by check or money order. Mailed requests are processed within two to three weeks. The Boston counter at One Ashburton Place does up to three documents per customer; Springfield and Fall River also have offices. [source](https://www.sec.state.ma.us/divisions/commissions/apostilles.htm)

The Secretary of the Commonwealth, Public Records Division, Commissions Section, is the office in Massachusetts authorized to issue an apostille or certification for a document going to a foreign country. If the destination country is a signatory to the Hague Convention, the certificate is called an apostille.

## At a glance

| Item | What the official page says |
| Issuing office | William Francis Galvin, Secretary of the Commonwealth, Public Records Division, Commissions Section [source](https://www.sec.state.ma.us/divisions/commissions/apostilles.htm) |
| Fee | $6.00 per document. Checks or money orders payable to the Commonwealth of Massachusetts. The official page and request form specify checks or money orders; the official brochure says cash is not recommended because the office cannot refund cash lost in transit. The request form says checks and money orders only. [source](https://www.sec.state.ma.us/divisions/commissions/apostilles.htm) [source](https://www.sec.state.ma.us/divisions/commissions/download/authentication-form.pdf) [source](https://www.sec.state.ma.us/divisions/commissions/download/apostille_and_certification_information.pdf) |
| Mail | Yes. Include the destination country, payment, a prepaid return envelope, and the documents. For FedEx, DHL, or another express service, enclose a prepaid return envelope with a billing account number. The office does not accept credit cards as pre-payment for express mail. [source](https://www.sec.state.ma.us/divisions/commissions/apostilles.htm) |
| Boston office | Commissions Section, Room 1719, One Ashburton Place, Boston, MA 02108. Phone (617) 727-2836; comm@sec.state.ma.us. The apostilles page also lists 1-800-392-6090 and cis@sec.state.ma.us. [source](https://www.sec.state.ma.us/divisions/commissions/apostilles.htm) |
| Regional offices | Springfield: 436 Dwight Street, Room 102, Springfield, MA 01103, (413) 784-1376. Fall River: 218 South Main Street, Suite 206, Fall River, MA 02721, (508) 646-1374. The official page says number of documents and turnaround times at regional offices will vary. [source](https://www.sec.state.ma.us/divisions/commissions/apostilles.htm) [source](https://www.sec.state.ma.us/divisions/commissions/download/authentication-form.pdf) |
| In person (Boston) | Up to three documents can be done per customer at the counter. If you have four or more documents, you can pick them up after 3 p.m. on the next business day. Any document dropped off after 4 p.m. must be picked up the next business day. “There will be no exceptions.” The request form restates that more than three hand-delivered documents must be left overnight and picked up the next business day, no exceptions. [source](https://www.sec.state.ma.us/divisions/commissions/apostilles.htm) |
| Mail processing time | Mailed requests are processed within two to three weeks. [source](https://www.sec.state.ma.us/divisions/commissions/apostilles.htm) |

## What documents can Massachusetts certify?
Certifications can only be obtained for documents with an original signature of a valid Massachusetts notary public, justice of the peace, city or town clerk or assistant, court clerk or assistant, or registrar of vital records. Photocopied signatures can’t be certified. [source](https://www.sec.state.ma.us/divisions/commissions/apostilles.htm)
The official brochure states that the Secretary’s office is the only office in Massachusetts authorized to issue an apostille or certification for a notarized document going to a foreign country, and that Massachusetts does not certify out-of-state documents; they must be certified by the state of origin. [source](https://www.sec.state.ma.us/divisions/commissions/download/apostille_and_certification_information.pdf)
The official request form adds that the office does not authenticate federal or out-of-state documents, and that it does not authenticate notarized photocopies of government-issued documents (its examples include a notarized photocopy of a Delaware certificate of good standing or of an FBI background check). [source](https://www.sec.state.ma.us/divisions/commissions/download/authentication-form.pdf)
Identify the destination country on the request. “Different countries require different types of certification. If the country is a signatory to the Hague Convention, the document will be called an apostille.” [source](https://www.sec.state.ma.us/divisions/commissions/apostilles.htm)
Rather not do this yourself?
Tell us the document, that it was issued in Massachusetts, and where it's going. We'll pass your request to an independent apostille service that can handle the whole thing, and they'll reply with a quote. It's free to ask and you're under no obligation.

# How to get an apostille in New York
Short answer: New York apostilles come from the Department of State's Apostille and Authentication Unit and cost $10 per document. Notarized papers and most county-issued vital records need a county clerk certification first. Mail the request to Albany, or use same-day walk-in service in New York City, Albany, Binghamton, Buffalo or Utica (up to 10 documents). [source](https://dos.ny.gov/apostille-certificate-authentication)

The New York Department of State authenticates public documents issued in New York State that are signed by a New York State official or county clerk. The same office issues either an apostille or a certificate of authentication, depending on the destination country.

## At a glance

| Item | What the official page says |
| Issuing office | New York Department of State, Division of Licensing Services, Apostille and Authentication Unit [source](https://dos.ny.gov/apostille-certificate-authentication) |
| Fee | $10 per document [source](https://dos.ny.gov/apostille-certificate-authentication) |
| Mail | Yes. Processed according to receipt date. Returned by first-class mail unless you enclose a prepaid overnight shipping label. The office does not accept labels that bill your credit card or “bill sender.” |
| Mailing address | New York Department of State, Division of Licensing Services, Apostille and Authentication Unit, PO Box 22001, Albany, NY 12201-2001. Express and next-day carriers should use the Albany physical address: 1 Commerce Plaza, 99 Washington Avenue, 6th Floor, Albany, NY 12231. [source](https://dos.ny.gov/apostille-certificate-authentication) |
| In person | Same-day walk-in service in New York City, Albany, Binghamton, Buffalo, and Utica. Limited to 10 documents per customer. Drop-off (not treated as a priority; processed by receipt date) is allowed only in Albany and New York City. |
| Mail processing time | — |

The official page does not publish a routine turnaround time for mailed or drop-off requests. We therefore show a dash rather than estimate one. [source](https://dos.ny.gov/apostille-certificate-authentication)

## Where can you get a same-day apostille in New York?
Walk-in same-day apostille and authentication services, as published: [source](https://dos.ny.gov/apostille-certificate-authentication)

- New York City, 123 William St., 2nd Fl., New York, NY 10038-3804, 9:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m.
- Albany, 1 Commerce Plaza, 99 Washington Avenue, 6th Floor, Albany, NY 12231, 9:00 a.m. to 4:15 p.m.
- Binghamton, State Office Building, 44 Hawley Street, Room 1506, Binghamton, NY 13901-4455, 9:00 a.m. to 12:00 p.m. and 12:45 p.m. to 4:00 p.m.
- Buffalo, 295 Main Street, 8th Floor, Suite 821, Buffalo, NY 14203, 9:00 a.m. to 12:00 p.m. and 12:45 p.m. to 4:00 p.m.
- Utica, State Office Building, 207 Genesee Street, Utica, NY 13501-2812, 9:00 a.m. to 12:00 p.m. and 12:45 p.m. to 4:00 p.m.
The Department of State call center is (518) 474-4429, 8:45 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. Monday through Friday except legal holidays. [source](https://dos.ny.gov/apostille-certificate-authentication)
Credit-card payments on mailed requests require a CVV on the current request form; the office says older forms without a CVV can cause the payment to be rejected and the documents returned. [source](https://dos.ny.gov/apostille-certificate-authentication)

## What has to happen before you file?
The Department of State only authenticates public documents issued in New York State and signed by a New York State official or county clerk. [source](https://dos.ny.gov/apostille-certificate-authentication)

- Birth, death, and marriage certificates and certificates of divorce issued by a local or county official, or a county department of health, must first be certified by the county clerk of the county where the document was issued.
- Vital records issued by the New York State Department of Health and bearing the signature of the Director of Vital Statistics or the NYS Registrar may be submitted without a county-clerk certification. The official page warns that the words “New York State,” “registrar,” or “vital records” on a local certificate do not, by themselves, mean it was issued by the State Department of Health.
- Notarized documents must be certified by the county clerk of the county where the notary is commissioned.
- A NYS criminal background check must be submitted with the cover letter bearing the signature of the Division of Criminal Justice Services representative. Federal/FBI background checks must be authenticated by the U.S. Department of State.

## Do you need an apostille or a certificate of authentication?
An apostille is issued under the 1961 Hague Convention for use in countries that have joined the Convention. A Certificate of Authentication is issued for use in a country that is not a member. The official page says Certificates of Authentication “may also require an additional certification from the United States Department of State prior to submission to the foreign country.” [source](https://dos.ny.gov/apostille-certificate-authentication)
Both certificates are described as a one-page document with a blue laser-printed facsimile of the Department of State seal and the facsimile signature of the Secretary of State or a deputy. Apostilles and certificates issued on or after April 9, 2013, may be verified through the Department’s online tool, linked from the official page. [source](https://dos.ny.gov/apostille-certificate-authentication)
Rather not do this yourself?
Tell us the document, that it was issued in New York, and where it's going. We'll pass your request to an independent apostille service that can handle the whole thing, and they'll reply with a quote. It's free to ask and you're under no obligation.

# How to get an apostille in Texas
Short answer: The Texas Secretary of State's Authentications Unit in Austin charges $15 per universal apostille ($10 for adoption documents, capped at $100 per child). It works as an apostille for Hague countries and as an authentication for others. In-person service is same-day for up to 10 documents; mailed requests can take up to two weeks. [source](https://www.sos.state.tx.us/authfaqs.shtml) [source](https://www.sos.texas.gov/statdoc/request.shtml)

The Texas Secretary of State, Authentications Unit, issues a “universal Apostille.” Officially, that certificate operates as an apostille for countries that are party to the Apostille Convention and as an authentication for countries that are not.

## At a glance

| Item | What the official page says |
| Issuing office | Office of the Texas Secretary of State, Authentications Unit, 400 West 15th Street, Austin, TX 78701 [source](https://www.sos.texas.gov/statdoc/request.shtml) |
| Fee | $15.00 per universal apostille, not per page. For an adoption, $10.00 per apostille, and total fees may not exceed $100.00 for the adoption of each child. Adoption requests use Form 2103. [source](https://www.sos.state.tx.us/authfaqs.shtml) |
| Mail | Yes, first come, first served. Include Form 2102, payment, and a prepaid return envelope. Credit-card payment is not accepted through the mail. [source](https://www.sos.texas.gov/statdoc/forms/2102new.pdf) |
| Mailing address | Authentications Unit, P.O. Box 13550, Austin, TX 78711-3550, as printed on official Form 2102. The physical address for walk-in and appointment service is 400 West 15th St., Austin, TX 78701. [source](https://www.sos.texas.gov/statdoc/forms/2102new.pdf) |
| In person | Same-day service for a maximum of 10 documents per person, company, or transaction. Appointments are required Tuesday through Thursday (one appointment per person or company per day). Walk-in service is Monday and Friday only, no appointment. Groups should be limited to no more than two people. The office will not pull a mailed request for walk-in service. [source](https://www.sos.texas.gov/statdoc/request.shtml) |
| Drop-off | More than 10 documents may be dropped off Monday through Friday for a three-day / 72-hour processing turnaround. Requests must be registered in the office’s QR drop-box system and must include the bulk drop-off form. [source](https://www.sos.texas.gov/statdoc/request.shtml) |
| Processing as published | In person: same day. Drop-off: within 72 hours / three days. Mail: “can take up to two weeks from the day of receipt”; “actual processing times may vary depending on volume.” The office also says “Please allow at least two weeks from the date we receive your documents for processing.” [source](https://www.sos.texas.gov/statdoc/request.shtml) |

## Hours and payment
The walk-in office is listed at 400 West 15th Street, Austin, TX 78701, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., Monday through Friday. The request page warns that in-person wait times may exceed an hour, and that the office was closed Wednesday, November 25, through Friday, November 27, 2026, for Thanksgiving — confirm current closures before you go. [source](https://www.sos.texas.gov/statdoc/request.shtml)
Walk-in payment may be by check, money order, credit or debit card, or cash with exact change. Mailed requests may be paid by check or money order drawn on a U.S. bank and payable to the Office of the Texas Secretary of State, or by funding an SOS client account. The FAQ says checks and money orders should be in favor of the “Secretary of State of Texas.” Personal checks or money orders missing the amount, the requestor’s complete address, or the payee’s signature will not be accepted. [source](https://www.sos.texas.gov/statdoc/request.shtml) [source](https://www.sos.state.tx.us/authfaqs.shtml)

## Which documents qualify for a Texas apostille?
All documents must be issued from the state of Texas or properly notarized by a Texas notary public. You must submit the original Texas-issued document, a Texas-issued certified copy, or an original Texas-notarized document. The office does not apostille copies of certified or notarized records, and it does not apostille documents for use within the United States or its territories. Certified records must have been issued within the past five years; the official page says documents older than five years may not be verifiable and cannot be apostilled. [source](https://www.sos.texas.gov/statdoc/request.shtml)
You must indicate the destination country on Form 2102. [source](https://www.sos.texas.gov/statdoc/request.shtml)
If the destination country is not a party to the Apostille Convention, the official FAQ says you “likely need to get your universal Apostille validated by the Office of Authentications with the U.S. State Department.” [source](https://www.sos.state.tx.us/authfaqs.shtml)

## Can Texas apostille a remote online (RON) notarization?
Texas will apostille an online (RON) notarization if you also present a notarization ledger (date and time signatures were applied, document description, and signer information) and a notarial certificate stating the document was notarized via “electronic or online notarization by two-way audio and visual communication.” The official page warns that some countries do not accept online notarized documents even after this office authenticates them. [source](https://www.sos.texas.gov/authinfo.shtml) See online notarization for apostille documents.
Rather not do this yourself?
Tell us the document, that it was issued in Texas, and where it's going. We'll pass your request to an independent apostille service that can handle the whole thing, and they'll reply with a quote. It's free to ask and you're under no obligation.
